title: Structured execution evidence to verified selective-computation bridge
question: At fixed terminal candidate budget B=8, does a target-blind activation-trace probe convert its measured information advantage into higher exact downstream verification success than the best scalar-output probe?
hypothesis: The activation-trace channel will produce substantially higher verified selective-computation success at M=512/B=8 than scalar output because its one-step evidence partitions leave far fewer compatible hypotheses.

arms.name: scalar_row
arms.intervention: choose one input row by deterministic maximum-information-per-environment-work selection; observe only the binary output

arms.name: activation_trace
arms.intervention: choose one input row by the same deterministic selector over ordered non-input activation bits; observe the full six-bit activation trace

endpoints.name: verified_success_delta_m512_b8
endpoints.role: primary — seed-level activation_trace minus scalar_row exact-verifier success difference at M=512/B=8

endpoints.name: verified_success
endpoints.role: secondary — exact verifier success across B=1/2/4/8 and all registered M levels

endpoints.name: target_bucket_size
endpoints.role: secondary — compatible candidates after the selected probe

endpoints.name: information_gain_bits
endpoints.role: secondary — one-step deterministic information under the selected channel

endpoints.name: expected_remaining_candidates
endpoints.role: secondary — collision expectation after the selected probe

endpoints.name: execution_work_fraction
endpoints.role: secondary — terminal verification work divided by exhaustive exact verification work

held_constant: same static 512-program evaluation library per seed

terminal_protocol.procedure: After selecting one probe without target identity, form the exact compatible evidence bucket from the realized target evidence, retain the first min(8,bucket_size) candidates in deterministic public library order, and run exact CASM verification against all 16 input rows.

cost_model.probe_environment: same G-CASM-015 exact graph execution plus trace read units
cost_model.terminal_verification: sum of exact executor work over shortlisted candidates and all 16 rows
cost_model.exhaustive_reference: same exact executor work over all M candidates and all 16 rows

leakage_rules: Probe selection uses only public candidate-predicted evidence and public action descriptors.
Target identity and target index are never supplied to selection.
Realized target evidence is unavailable until after the action is selected.
Exact verifier rows are not available to the selector.
No result from 016C is used to alter probe definitions or the terminal budget.

decision_rule.condition: Primary activation_trace minus scalar_row CI is positive and excludes zero at M=512/B=8.
decision_rule.licenses: evidence that structured execution evidence translates into higher verified selective-computation capability on the finite registered workload.
decision_rule.does_not_license: learned probe policy, asymptotic scaling, arbitrary internal-state access, or multimodal competence.

decision_rule.condition: Trace increases information but not verified success.
decision_rule.licenses: the observation channel is informative but downstream evidence-to-action translation remains limiting.

decision_rule.condition: Trace and scalar verified success are similar.
decision_rule.licenses: the measured information advantage does not automatically translate into terminal capability under B=8.
decision_rule.does_not_license: failure of other structured evidence channels.
